# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 71 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 71 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_071_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 71 begins the systematic interpretation of the rod categories established in chapter 70. The shepherd explains five categories in this chapter, moving from worst (apostates) to progressively better states.

The category of apostates (*apostasantes*) in 71:1 is the most severe — those who "blasphemed the Lord in their sins" and "were ashamed of the name of the Lord invoked upon them." The phrase *to onoma tou kyriou to epiklēthen ep' autous* — "the name of the Lord called/invoked upon them" — refers to baptism, where the name of the Lord was pronounced over the candidate. These people are *nekroi eis ton theon* — "dead to God."

The "towers" referenced in 71:4-5 (first tower, second tower, third tower) connect back to the tower-building vision in the Visions section of Hermas (Vis. 3). The towers represent different levels or ranks of salvation/placement. The reference assumes the reader knows the earlier vision.

The term *dipsychoi* ("double-minded") appears again in 71:4, consistent with Hermas's characteristic usage. All agents render this as "double-minded." SOPHIA maintains this rendering.

The description of wealthy faithful in 71:5 as "ashamed of the truth" is a sharp social critique — wealth and worldly entanglement produce theological embarrassment before the confession of Christ.

All three agents agree substantially. Main disagreements involve "life has departed" vs. "life has withdrawn," and the handling of the tower references.

---

## Similitude 8, Part 2 — The Meaning of the Rods

**71:1** "Those whose rods were found withered and moth-eaten — these are the apostates and betrayers of the church, who blasphemed the Lord in their sins and were also ashamed of the name of the Lord which was called upon them. These people are utterly dead to God. And you see that not one of them repented, even though they heard the words which you proclaimed to them. From such people life has departed."

**71:2** "But those who surrendered rods that were dry and cracked — these too are close to the apostates. They did not apostatize, but they never bore fruit. For just as a dry rod bears no fruit, so also these people do live, but they bear no fruit of any good work. Their repentance, however, remains possible for them, if they repent quickly. But if they delay, they too will share in the death of the first group."

**71:3** "Lord," I said, "why is repentance still possible for them, but not for the first group? Their rods were just as similar." "For this reason repentance is still possible for them," he said — "they did not blaspheme their Lord, nor did they become betrayers of the church. But through desire for gain they deceived and each one served his own desires. Let them repent, therefore."

**71:4** "Those who surrendered rods half-dry and cracked — hear about them. Those who are perpetually double-minded and who speak evil of one another — these are those whose rods were half-dry. Many of them repented when they heard my commandments, and those who repented were given a dwelling in the first tower. But those who repented more slowly were given a dwelling in the second tower."

**71:5** "Those who surrendered their rods green but dried at the tips — these are those who were faithful but wealthy, and who were immersed in the affairs of this age. They are ashamed of the truth. Some of these, when they heard my commandments, repented and were found good. The rest remain in their affairs and are cut off from the holy ones. These will find entry to the place of the third tower difficult."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
